pages.text: Technology is unlocked $(bold)per player$(). Killing a boss does not unlock it for the server: it drops $(bold)Blueprints$(), one for every player who fought, plus one spare.$(br2)Use a Blueprint and you learn that technology. The spare is for someone who was not there.

Blueprints are ordinary items: trade them, sell them, gift them, or take them off a corpse. A new player on an old server catches up by trading, not by grinding the same boss.$(br2)Stuck on a boss? Every Blueprint also has a $(bold)charter$() recipe: expensive, emerald-priced, and always available. Slow, but never blocked.

Recipes you have not learned are $(bold)visible but locked$(): EMI shows them, the tooltip names the boss. Gated blocks check too: a brass machine handed to someone who has not learned brass will not run for them.$(br2)Players who want to share progress can form a team; a team's Blueprint teaches the team.

A Blueprint is a blue sheet that names its technology. Right-click to learn it; it is used up. Hover any locked item and the tooltip names the Blueprint and the boss.$(br2)The ladder is four tiers. Each tier is a kind of fight, not a difficulty number.
